## What changed

**Notifications that were never going to arrive said nothing about it.** A
Telegram channel needs both a token and a chat id; with only one of them
`channelsFrom` returns nothing, the notifier becomes a no-op stub, and the
whole thing stays silent. You find out at the worst possible moment — waiting
for word that a nineteen-step climb has stopped, on a run you deliberately
detached so you would not have to watch it.

Readiness now says which of the three states you are in, before the climb
rather than after:

```
✓  уведомления  настроены: telegram
!  уведомления  настроено наполовину: не хватает telegram-chat.
                Канал не сработает и не скажет об этом
✓  уведомления  не настроены — о падении узнаете только из attach
```

Only the half-configured case is a warning, and it carries the command that
fixes it in one go (`gitlab-upgrade notify chat --yes`). Having no channel at
all is a choice, not a defect, so it does not demand `--force` — it is simply
no longer invisible. A profile that sends nothing at all (nothing to upgrade)
says so instead of pretending a channel is missing; note that even a patch
reports failures, so it wants a channel too.
